analysis:
The change touches only docs/architecture/inference.md (timestamp bump, a new cluster heartbeat health-file paragraph, and a rewrite of the cluster runtime-facts intro). No source code or enforced control changed. The head excerpts I received (lines 1-837) cover mostly pre-existing text. Of the changed ranges, only the line 3 timestamp falls in them. The new health-file paragraph (head ~3528-3536) and the runtime-facts rewrite (~5230+) lie outside the supplied excerpts, so I judged them from the patch hunks only.

Security-relevant observations:
(1) Heartbeat paragraph: DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_MEMBER_HEALTH_FILE with separate service-health.json and part-health.json, and a supervisor liveness guard that accepts only the service's own PID. This describes a local availability/integrity hardening and does not weaken TB-012, TB-013 or any provider-to-coordinator control. The documented guard (PID-bound heartbeat) is a mitigation, not a regression. I did not verify the implementation. It touches availability of cluster serving (A-018) only.
(2) Runtime-facts rewrite: a signed release computes the digests of its approvals from its own final app and registers them (cluster_runtime). This relates to the A-016/A-017 build-qualification and T-054 'stale code evidence' theme. I could not verify from the supplied evidence that the release-lane registration is authenticated or independently approved, since the code and the operations/provider-release.md doc were not supplied. The doc claim is a threat-model-relevant contract that the integration pass and the platform should confirm; it is not a finding here.
(3) The visible unchanged text on prefix cache (encrypted SSD checkpoints, authenticated tenant cache scope) is consistent with T-041 and unchanged by this PR. The prefix-cache text states that an image request with a cache scope reuses only within an identity of its features, and that without a scope it stays cold and never publishes.

No new attack surface or threat-model invalidation is evident from documentation-only changes. The remaining question is whether the new cluster_runtime registration path has a code-level authorization boundary, which is outside the supplied evidence.
